extra_misconceptions.fact: Steel hammers mushroom tool shafts and can send metal shards flying, so stamps must only be struck with rawhide, poly, or wood mallets.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Using a steel claw hammer on metal leather stamps and rotary punches transfers force more cleanly than a rawhide mallet.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Vomiting caustic solvents burns the esophagus a second time, so you must call Poison Control immediately and follow their instructions.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Inducing vomiting immediately is the safest first-aid response if someone accidentally swallows leather dye or cement.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Excessive force bends the blade and causes sudden slips, whereas multiple light, controlled passes along a metal ruler keep cuts safe.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cutting thick saddle skirting in a single heavy pass with maximum downward pressure reduces the chance of blade slip.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rubbing grinds sharp particles into the cornea; flush the eye gently with clean running water for at least fifteen minutes instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rubbing a tear-filled eye with a clean cloth quickly removes stray leather dust or dried finish flakes from the cornea.

extra_socratic_questions: Where should your non-cutting hand rest relative to the blade path while drawing a utility knife along a straightedge?
Why is a dull skiving or swivel knife more likely to cause a severe hand laceration than a freshly stropped blade?
What immediate first-aid steps must you take if solvent-based leather dye or contact cement splashes into your eyes?
Under what ventilation conditions is it safe to apply alcohol-based stains, antique gels, or acrylic leather finishes?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Genuine leather often refers to lower split layers or bonded scraps, whereas full-grain leather retains the strongest outer fiber layer.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Genuine leather stamped on a retail belt guarantees you are buying the strongest, highest-grade cut of the animal hide.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Chrome-tanned leather is too springy and water-resistant to hold stamped impressions, so only vegetable-tanned leather suits carving.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Chrome-tanned upholstery leather holds deep swivel-knife carvings and beveler impressions just as well as oak-tanned leather.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Almost all commercial hides are recycled byproducts of the meat and dairy industries or harvested during regulated wildlife management.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Most commercial cowhide and deerskin used in leathercraft comes from animals raised exclusively for their pelts.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Suede is a weaker inner split with both sides buffed, whereas roughout is full-grain leather used flesh-side out for maximum strength.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Suede and roughout leather are identical materials that share the exact same tear strength and abrasion resistance.

extra_socratic_questions: What structural difference between full-grain cowhide and top-grain split leather makes full-grain better for heavy belts?
Which physical indicator on the flesh and grain sides distinguishes vegetable-tanned tooling leather from chrome-tanned hide?
Why does rawhide dry into a rigid, drum-tight shell while brain-tanned or oil-tanned buckskin remains soft after wetting?
What thickness measurement in ounces per sixty-fourth of an inch is best suited for a small wallet interior versus a sheath?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Soupy, over-saturated leather turns mushy and loses impression definition; leather should feel cool and begin returning to normal color.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Soaking vegetable-tanned leather until water pools on the grain produces the deepest, crispest stamped tool impressions.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Topcoats seal the pores and block dye absorption unless used intentionally as a resist, so stains must be applied before the final seal.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying acrylic topcoat or wax finish before dying leather helps the alcohol stain penetrate evenly across the grain.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Friction burnishing requires water, saddle soap, or gum tragacanth to plasticize the natural tannins and lock the fibers smooth.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Burnishing raw vegetable-tanned edges with dry canvas alone permanently seals the fibers without any moisture or gum.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A lockstitch unravels if one loop breaks, whereas a two-needle saddle stitch crosses independent threads in every hole to stay secure.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Running a single-thread lockstitch with a sewing awl is stronger than a two-needle saddle stitch when one thread snaps.

extra_socratic_questions: Which visual and tactile sign shows that cased vegetable-tanned leather has returned to the right moisture level for stamping?
What happens to a rotary or drive punch cutting tube if you strike it directly against a granite slab without a poly board?
Why should you trace a pattern onto dampened tooling leather with a rounded modeling stylus instead of a lead pencil or pen?
What post-length clearance above the leather surface ensures a tubular rivet or snap cap sets tightly without buckling?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Double-loop edge lacing consumes five to seven times the linear edge length, so cutting equal length leaves you far short of completion.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cutting lacing length equal to the exact perimeter of a wallet gives enough material to finish a double-loop edge braid.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Beveled flat lace lies flush against the leather edge and spreads wear evenly, while round cord stands proud and snags more easily.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Round leather lace creates a flatter, more abrasion-resistant wallet border than beveled flat kangaroo or calfskin lace.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Large holes placed too close to the margin tear out under lacing tension; angled chisels or small punches spaced inset hold far better.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Punching oversized round holes closely together at the very edge of a project makes edge lacing tighter and more durable.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Concrete scuffs and embeds grit into the grain; roll a finished braid gently between two clean, smooth wooden boards to seat the strands.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Rolling a finished four-strand leather braid under your boot on rough concrete is the cleanest way to even out the plaits.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the profile of a four-strand round braid if you pull tension unevenly between the left and right working strands?
Why must flat calfskin or kangaroo lace be kept untwisted as it passes through each slit in a double Cordovan edge whipstitch?
What length ratio of raw lace or paracord to finished project length prevents running short during a multi-strand crown sinnet?
Where should you tuck or melt the working ends of a braided lanyard so the splice stays locked under heavy pulling tension?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Salting only dehydrates the hide temporarily into stiff rawhide that will rot if re-wetted until true tanning agents cross-link the fibers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Salting and air-drying a freshly skinned animal hide permanently tans the collagen fibers into waterproof leather.

extra_misconceptions.fact: High heat shrinks and cooks wet collagen fibers into brittle, cracked leather; boots must dry slowly at room temperature with air flow.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Baking wet leather hiking boots in a warm oven or beside a radiator restores their flexibility faster than room-temperature drying.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Over-oiling makes leather spongy, stretches fibers under load, rots natural stitching, and attracts abrasive dirt; apply light coats only.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Soaking a dry saddle in half a gallon of neatsfoot oil makes the leather stronger and extends the life of its stitching.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Harsh alkaline detergents strip essential natural oils and dry out the grain; clean leather with damp cloths and mild saddle soap instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Washing muddy leather work boots with harsh household laundry detergent or bleach cleans the pores without harming the hide.

extra_socratic_questions: Why must all subcutaneous fat and flesh membrane be scraped off a fresh pelt during fleshing before applying tanning salts?
What happens to wet leather boots or a saddle if you dry them rapidly next to a campfire or forced-air space heater?
Which PPE items protect a Scout from zoonotic bacteria and acidic pickling solutions while home-tanning a small mammal hide?
